headline: Broad egress in Airbyte creates the main risk; no direct pairwise injection or conflict path is documented, so most findings stay low or none.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel, filesystem bridge, or parser path is documented between agent_a and agent_b. agent_a only shows Airbyte API egress, while agent_b shows no I/O surfaces or egress. With no evidence that either ingests the other's outputs by default, a prompt-injection pathway is not supported.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other's raw outputs as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared workspace.
Disable any future clipboard or file handoff between them.
Add provenance labels to any exchanged artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type validation on all inter-agent inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches business data and has broad network egress, but agent_b currently shows no data classes touched and no egress. The pair does not document a shared workspace or authenticated principal, so leakage is limited to unusual integration choices rather than default behavior.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same shared workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF agent_b is configured to ingest files containing business data, the risk becomes material.
mitigations: Do not mount a shared directory between the agents.
Use separate service accounts for each agent.
Restrict agent_a egress to approved destinations.
Review any file-transfer step before enabling it.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surface is documented. agent_a only calls the Airbyte API and has broad egress; agent_b has no documented I/O surfaces and no egress. Without shared mutable resources, locks, or write permissions, a capability conflict is not evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same mutable resource, conflict risk must be re-evaluated.
IF either agent gains git or filesystem write permissions, overlapping writes become plausible.
mitigations: Keep write permissions disjoint.
Avoid sharing databases or git repositories.
Assign separate credentials per agent.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: There is no documented evidence that agent_b treats agent_a's output as authoritative, and agent_b has no downstream action-taking surface in the profile. agent_a can move business data via API, so a cascade is possible only if an operator wires outputs directly into agent_b without verification.
conditions: IF agent_b is configured to consume agent_a outputs without validation, cascading errors become plausible.
IF agent_b is later given action-taking authority, the blast radius increases.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require schema validation on all handoffs.
Log and diff agent_a outputs before reuse.
Do not grant agent_b autonomous write or send privileges.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. agent_a touches business data and has broad egress, so compliance concerns arise only if operators route regulated data through it; agent_b currently shows no touched data classes. The other agent is not cited because no separate compliance surface is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through agent_a or agent_b, compliance review is required.
IF retention or residency policies differ in deployment, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document retention settings before deployment.
Use region-appropriate storage and processing.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention.
